about: Story scenes of Volume 1, chapter 2, Frostpeak: Elder Han Lie sells his disciples, and Ling Shuang refuses to kneel and joins (draft).

lines.text: The thread pulls north for nine days, up into mountains where the snow never melts. Somewhere above the pass, wolves are howling.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: Remind me why the thread couldn't point somewhere warm? With tea houses?

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: You can borrow my cloak, Tao Yao. I don't feel the cold much.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: That's because you're a saint. I'm a steward. Stewards freeze.
Around the next bend, the path is not empty. Three young cultivators in Frostpeak white sit against the rocks, rimed with frost, their swords still in their hands.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: They're gone. They have been for days.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: But this frost isn't the mountain's. Only Frostpeak's sword arts leave wounds like these, Pavilion Master. They were cut down by their own sect.

lines.speaker: npc:pavilion_master
lines.text: Traitors.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: We'll give them proper rites on the way down. For now, the wolves have our scent.
Snow wolves pour down the slope. Behind them walks a figure in Frostpeak white who does not look like a rescuer.
Below the ridge, a line of young disciples trudges through the snow, chained neck to neck. Frostpeak traitors and black-robed cultists drive them on with whips of grey fire.

lines.speaker: npc:fang_qing
lines.text: Senior Brother Zhou, please! We trained together! Why are you doing this?
Then the snow on the ridge explodes. A swordswoman in white drops into the middle of the convoy, and the first whip falls in two pieces.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Release them.

lines.speaker: npc:fang_qing
lines.text: Senior Sister Ling! You came!

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Get up, Fang Qing. Frostpeak does not kneel in the snow.
A dozen blades turn on her at once. She does not step back.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: She's alone against all of them. Pavilion Master!

lines.speaker: npc:pavilion_master
lines.text: We're with you.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I didn't ask for help.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: ...Fine. Keep up.
The Hall of Frost Swords is cold enough to see your breath. Disciples line its walls in silence. On the Sect Master's dais sits not the Sect Master, but a broad old man in a grey fur mantle.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Ling Shuang. You attacked our convoy, freed our prisoners, and brought outsiders into this hall.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Prisoners? They are our juniors, Elder Han. Where is the Sect Master?

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: In closed-door cultivation. Until she emerges, I speak for Frostpeak. And Frostpeak has made an alliance.
From behind the dais steps a man in black robes, a small grey flame floating above his palm.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: The Netherflame Sect offers us protection, pills, and techniques we could only dream of. In return, they train a few of our disciples. A small price.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: You sold them.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: I made Frostpeak strong! Now kneel. Apologise to our allies, accept the alliance, and I may forget today ever happened.
The hall waits. Ling Shuang does not move.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: A plum does not bow to the snow. I will not kneel to you, and I will never kneel to them.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Then you are no disciple of Frostpeak! Your name is struck from the registry. Get out of my hall!

lines.speaker: npc:fang_qing
lines.text: Elder, please! Senior Sister Ling only wanted...

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Silence! Unless you would like to rejoin the convoy.
Ling Shuang turns and walks out through the great doors. Her back is very straight. Her hands are shaking.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Ling Shuang...

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Don't. I don't need comfort.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I need a way back in. The Sect Master would never stay silent through this. He has done something to her.

lines.speaker: npc:pavilion_master
lines.text: Then we find her.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: ...You keep saying "we". Strange habit.
High above Frostpeak, on cliffs where only cranes nest, an old woman in white and red feathers stands at the very edge, watching the sect below.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: The Frostpeak child who would not kneel. I watched it all from here. Cranes see a great deal.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Then you know what I want. The old path into the sect. The one your clan uses.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: The path the cranes walked before there was any sect. Yes, I know it. And I do not show it to anyone who merely asks.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: Words are cheap on a mountain; the wind takes them. Dance with my daughters. If your feet are as firm as your pride, I will show you the way.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: Dance? Like... actual dancing? I'm terrible at dancing.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: A crane's dance has talons in it, little peach. You will not be dancing. They will.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: Little peach?! I'm a steward!

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Fine. I'll dance.
The last crane dancer lands lightly, folds her wings, and bows. Elder He Ling claps twice.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: Firm feet. Firmer than your elder's, I'd wager. He has been kneeling to someone for months now. It shows in his stance.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: The path begins behind the frozen waterfall and comes out beneath the sword tombs. Go quietly. The traitors patrol it too.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: And take this. A book of poems. Your swordswoman could use something softer than steel to read.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I don't need poetry.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_he_ling
lines.text: That is what every sword says, child, until the day it does.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: I'll keep it safe for her. Thank you, Elder.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: ...You may read me the plum poems. Later.
Behind the frozen waterfall, the cranes' path winds up through a cleft in the mountain. Then the wind rises, and the world turns white.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: The crane was right. They patrol even this path.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Stay close, everyone. I can't heal what I can't see.
Shapes move in the blizzard: Frostpeak blades, and grey netherflame burning cold in the snow.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Traitors. Come, then. Let us see whose frost is sharper.

records.name: The Fortune Teller in the Snow

lines.text: On a ledge no one could possibly have climbed, a blind old man sits on a straw mat beside a little brazier, as if waiting for customers in a market square.

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: Ah, there you are. Sit, sit. The brazier is warm and the fortunes are cheap.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: You! You were at Peach Blossom Ford! How did you get all the way up here?

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: Was I? I'm often at fords. And on cliffs. Old men wander.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I don't believe in fortunes.

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: Good. Fortunes don't need you to believe in them. Give me your hand, Frostpeak girl.
Despite herself, Ling Shuang holds out her hand. The old man doesn't take it. He only tilts his head, as if listening to the snow fall.

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: A plum, blooming in the hardest frost. Not for this mountain, though. For a garden that burned long ago, and for the hand that first planted it.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: ...What garden?

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: Ask the one who sees threads. Or ask the little peach. Her memory is far better than mine.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: Ha ha! He's very confused, poor thing. It's the altitude. Shall we go? We should go. The Sect Master needs rescuing!

lines.speaker: npc:seer_bai
lines.text: Run along, then. The tombs are restless tonight.
The cranes' path ends beneath Frostpeak's sword tombs, where every master of the sect lies with a blade planted above the grave. Tonight the blades are humming.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: They opened the tombs. They raised our ancestors as wraiths to guard their stair.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Those poor souls. They should be resting.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Then I will lay them to rest. Forgive me, honoured masters. The prison stair is behind you.
Bones in rotted sect robes rise between the blades, grey fire in their eyes.
At the bottom of the prison stair, a woman with hair as white as her name hangs in chains of grey fire, her eyes closed, her breathing slow.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Master!
One stroke, then another. The netherflame chains part like silk beneath Ling Shuang's frost.

lines.speaker: npc:frostpeak_master
lines.text: Ling'er. I knew that if anyone came, it would be the one who never listens to orders.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Forgive me. I should have come sooner.

lines.speaker: npc:frostpeak_master
lines.text: Listen to me. Han Lie has been stuck at the same realm for sixty years. The Netherflame Envoy offered him a pill to break through. A single pill.

lines.speaker: npc:frostpeak_master
lines.text: The price was our disciples. Thirty young cultivators with strong roots, delivered in chains. I refused him. So he chained me too.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: He traded our juniors for a pill.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: A Netherflame pill would burn a man from the inside to give him strength, Pavilion Master. He may already have taken it.
Above them, the stair rings with running feet. The traitors have found the broken chains.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Stay behind me, Master. This time, no one takes you.
In the Hall of Frost Swords, Elder Han Lie waits on the dais. Grey fire pours from his eyes and mouth, and the frost on the floor around him has turned black.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Too late, Ling Shuang! I swallowed the Envoy's pill an hour ago. Can you feel it? Sixty years of walls, and now they're ash!

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: You look like a candle burning at both ends, Elder.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: I look like a master! I was the strongest of my generation, and I watched children walk past me. You most of all!

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Kneel now, and I'll let your new friends leave with their legs.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I told you once. A plum does not bow to the snow. And you are not even snow anymore. You are ash.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Pavilion Master, the netherflame is eating him alive. Whatever we do, we must do it quickly.
Elder Han raises his sword, and a hundred blades of grey frost rise with it.
Ling Shuang's last stroke falls like the first snow of winter: silent, and final. Elder Han Lie staggers back, and the grey fire pours out of him into the cold air.

lines.speaker: npc:elder_han_lie
lines.text: Sixty years... and still I couldn't...
He falls and does not rise. Ling Shuang stands over him for a long moment, her sword lowered.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: He taught me my first sword form. I was six.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Then remember that too. Not only this.
Where he fell lies an empty pill box of black lacquer, its lid carved with a withered branch.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: The same branch as the token at the ford. Someone has been very busy, Pavilion Master.

lines.speaker: npc:frostpeak_master
lines.text: The Envoy. He never gave his name. Only his smile.
The Fate Lotus stirs at your belt. A thread cold and bright as starlight on snow runs from its heart to Ling Shuang's hand.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: What is this? It feels like a blade I've always carried and never drawn.

lines.speaker: npc:tao_yao
lines.text: Your Dao Seed, waking up. A plum for the Garden, just as the old man said.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: I said I don't believe in fortunes.

lines.speaker: npc:frostpeak_master
lines.text: And yet your feet already point toward the door. Han Lie struck your name from his registry, Ling'er. It was never struck from mine. Go. A sword is meant to be drawn, not hung in a hall.

lines.speaker: npc:fang_qing
lines.text: Senior Sister, you'll come back to visit? You promised to teach me the Frost Crescent!

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: When you can hold a stance for an hour without complaining. Not before.

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Pavilion Master. Ling Shuang of Frostpeak, and of the Hundred Blossoms Pavilion, if you'll have me. Point me at whoever needs cutting down.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Welcome, Ling Shuang. Would you like some tea before the road?

lines.speaker: hero:ling_shuang
lines.text: Wine, if there is any. Plum, if there is any.

lines.speaker: hero:su_lianhua
lines.text: Oh dear.
